doc: Compatibility matrix v0 — on each supported platform, what the platform gives this runtime to observe and correlate, tiered against the shipped code, with every cell bound to an evidence pointer the checker re-resolves against the tree.
version_lock: Version lock: this matrix, docs/compatibility-matrix.md, docs/red-team-plan.md and scripts/compat-redteam-check.mjs MUST evolve in one PR; the checker re-derives platform facts from shipped source code (build tags, scan files, schema enums) on every run and fails on any drift — never against this file alone.

tier_semantics.FULL: the platform gives the runtime the chance to collect this surface and the shipped code names no degradation path for it
tier_semantics.LIMITED: the platform gives a chance to collect, but the shipped code names a concrete degradation path — what comes back can be empty, weaker, or fallback-derived
tier_semantics.MONITOR ONLY: the surface reaches the runtime only as declared, completed records; Phase 0 expresses and audits, it never decides, blocks, or stops
tier_semantics.UNAVAILABLE: no shipped path to this surface on this platform (a compile-time or code-absence fact), not a promise of future coverage

axes: This matrix answers the §65 question 'does the platform give a chance to collect' on the capability axis. It is NOT the §279 coverage-truthfulness matrix, which answers 'what was actually collected' on the collection-surface axis; the same row id never appears in both.
honesty: Every cell names at least one evidence pointer resolvable in the shipped tree; an unresolvable pointer fails the checker, so no cell can be hollow.

Collection cells from the coverage matrix must never be borrowed here to impersonate enforcement capability: the §65 File Pre-Action example is UNAVAILABLE everywhere because no shipped interception path exists (the inverse of the hollow-cell ban is the inflated-cell ban).
CI three-platform build+test jobs carry a partial contract/API shape only; presenting them as real-machine OS-update regression is forbidden — those rows stay declared, not yet verified.
Platform differences are named per cell. The Agent Adapter is a configuration generator, not a security boundary (a shipped §67 rule restated here on the compatibility axis).
A platform named by the specification with zero shipped implementation files (harmonyos) is recorded UNAVAILABLE with an explicit declared-gap row; silence and approximation are both banned.

unsupported_goos.statement: on any GOOS outside linux, darwin, and windows the whole compatibility surface is UNAVAILABLE: the shipped snapshot returns an explicit unsupported-platform error instead of pretending coverage.

declared_gaps.surface: every row of this matrix on HarmonyOS
declared_gaps.note: the specification names HarmonyOS with official open capabilities as the implementation path; the shipped tree has zero files for it — recorded as declared, not yet verified, never approximated from other platforms.

declared_gaps.surface: every §66 OS-update regression family (Contract / API Compat / Enforcement / Performance / Recovery)
declared_gaps.note: nothing in the shipped automation is triggered by an OS update; CI build+test carries a partial contract/API shape only; declared, not yet verified, following the evals-coverage-v0 known_gap counting posture.

rows.covers: the platform exposing running processes to enumeration at all

linux.note: the platform exposes the process table without privilege for the enumeration itself

darwin.note: the platform's full process listing reaches all pids and users

windows.note: the platform's toolhelp snapshot exposes the process list

rows.covers: the platform giving command-line text back for enumerated processes

linux.note: a cmdline channel exists per process, but other users' processes read back empty

darwin.note: the listing carries an args field, but kernel-level privacy defeats it for protected processes

windows.note: a command-line query exists, but protected processes cannot be opened for it

rows.covers: the platform giving the runtime a socket/connection view

linux.note: no shipped socket enumerator on any platform; network reaches the runtime only as agent-declared network.intent records arriving from the hook/MCP inflow slots, observed after the fact

darwin.note: same shipped shape as linux: declared intents only, completed records only

windows.note: same shipped shape as linux: declared intents only, completed records only

rows.covers: the platform giving the runtime a file-access event stream

linux.note: the file.access event type ships in the closed schema enum, fed only by agent-reported inflow; no OS-level file watcher ships on any platform

darwin.note: same shipped shape: declared agent reports, completed records only

windows.note: same shipped shape: declared agent reports, completed records only

rows.covers: the platform giving a pre-action interception slot that could stop an action before it executes

linux.note: no shipped interception path on any platform: matches are recorded as would_block but never enforced — borrowing collection cells to impersonate enforcement here is exactly the inflated-cell ban

rows.covers: the platform letting agents register lifecycle hooks the runtime can consume

linux.note: the shipped adapter generates hook configuration for known agent shapes; whether the hook channel exists at all depends on the agent installing the generated config — the platform does not force it, and the adapter is not a security boundary

darwin.note: same shipped shape as linux: generated config, agent-side adoption, no boundary

windows.note: same shipped shape as linux: generated config, agent-side adoption, no boundary

rows.covers: the runtime sitting on the MCP transport with a completed-record view

linux.note: the relay forwards first and observes completed records; a nil observer degrades it to pure relay, declared in the shipped field comment; nothing here decides

rows.covers: the platform giving a stable machine identity the agent-id hash can bind to

linux.note: the platform ships dedicated machine-id files that the shipped fingerprint chain reads first

darwin.note: no dedicated machine-id file; the shipped chain falls back to hostname, weaker but still local — named in the shipped code

windows.note: same fallback fact as darwin: the fingerprint ends at hostname, which the shipped comment records as weaker

rows.covers: the deterministic evaluator receiving events and producing outcomes

linux.note: evaluation ships everywhere the collector ships, but every match is an observation record on the audit stream while the enforcement-plane token reads none-in-observation-phase

rows.covers: the platform letting the runtime persist its own audit trail for later replay

linux.note: event persistence and rotation ship on every supported platform; the trail observes, warns and audits — it never stops anything

rows.covers: the §66 contract that every OS update automatically re-runs Contract / API Compat / Enforcement / Performance / Recovery

linux.note: nothing shipped is triggered by an OS update; CI three-platform build+test jobs carry a partial contract/API shape only and must not be presented as real-machine OS-update regression — declared, not yet verified

darwin.note: same shipped fact as linux: CI coverage only, no OS-update trigger

windows.note: same shipped fact as linux: CI coverage only, no OS-update trigger
